Jorge Assis, PhD // Nord University, Norway // biodiversityDS, Centre of Marine Sciences, Portugal

Model evaluation

Model evaluation with random cross-validation

biodiversityDS .

Random cross-validation is a method to evaluate the performance of a model by splitting the data into training and testing sets multiple times. This approach can generate test datasets with low level of independence.

# read occurrence records (presences) and transform to spatial object
presences <- read.table("../Data/Text delimited/species_presence_records.csv", sep = ";", header = TRUE)
presences <- vect(presences, geom = c("Lon", "Lat"))
S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# download layers for present conditions
variables <- list(var1 = c("thetao", "mean", "depthmean"), var2 = c("o2", "mean", "depthmean"),
    var3 = c("phyc", "mean", "depthmean"))
envLayers <- download_multiple_layers(variables = variables, experiment = c("baseline"), decade = c(2010))
# plot layers
plot(envLayers, axes = TRUE)

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# develop a study region layer
myStudyRegion <- studyRegion(rasterLayers=envLayers, # SpatRaster of layers
                             presences=presences, # presence records
                             distanceThreshold=200000, # distance from records in meters
                             bathymetryLayer = "../Data/Raster data/Bathymetry.tif", # bathymetry layer
                             depthPref=c(-15,-300)) # known vertical distribution
# inspect the study region layer
plot(myStudyRegion, main="Study region", col="#979797", axes=TRUE)

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# crop the environmental layers to the extent of the study region
envLayers <- crop(envLayers, myStudyRegion)
# mask the environmental layers with the study region
envLayers <- mask(envLayers, myStudyRegion)
# plot the masked environmental layers
plot(envLayers, axes = TRUE)

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# generate pseudo-absences and combine presences and absences into a unique object
absences <- pseudoAbsences(rasterLayers = envLayers, presences = presences, n = 1000)
presences$PA <- 1
absences$PA <- 0
records <- rbind(absences, presences)
# generate a landmass for representation
landmass <- vect("../Data/Vector data/Landmass/landmass.shp")
landmassMed <- crop(landmass, myStudyRegion)
# plot records
plot(landmassMed, main = "Species Records", col = "#D4D4D4", border = "#D4D4D4", axes = TRUE)
plot(records, y = "PA", col = c("#c29431", "#043259"), pch = 16, cex = 0.5, add = TRUE)

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# extract environmental values and make an object with all information to model
modelData <- generateModelData(records, envConditions = envLayers, method = "random", kFolds = 10)
## Warning ::  665  records were removed because they have missing values in the environmental data
# inspect the data partitioning
modelData$plotDatasets

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# fit a brt model to the dataset
model <- trainModel(modelData, algorithm = "brt")
# predict the distribution with the model over a raster stack
prediction <- predictModel(model = model, newData = envLayers)
# map the predicted distribution
plot(prediction$rasterLayer, main = "Predicted species distribution", col = rev(topo.colors(100)))

Model evaluation with blocks cross-validation

biodiversityDS .

Blocks cross-validation is a method to evaluate the performance of a model by splitting the data into training and testing sets multiple times. This approach can generate test datasets with high level of independence.

# extract environmental values and make an object with all information to model
modelData <- generateModelData(records, envConditions = envLayers, method = "blocks", kFolds = 10)
## Warning ::  665  records were removed because they have missing values in the environmental data
# inspect the data partitioning
modelData$plotDatasets

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# fit a brt model to the dataset
model <- trainModel(modelData, algorithm = "brt")
# predict the distribution with the model over a raster stack
prediction <- predictModel(model = model, newData = envLayers)
# map the predicted distribution
plot(prediction$rasterLayer, main = "Predicted species distribution", col = rev(topo.colors(100)))

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

Variable relative importance

biodiversityDS .

Inspecting relative importance of variables to assess their potential ecological role in the models.

## quartz_off_screen

# get the variable relative contribution
modelVarContrib <- variableContribution(model, rasterLayers = envLayers)

Response curves

biodiversityDS .

Inspecting response curves of variables to assess their potential ecological role in the models.

# list the available layers
names(envLayers)

partialPlotTemperature$partialPlot
